In creating the backstory for the client, let's call them Jordan. Jordan is a 32-year-old software developer from Seattle. They had a stable upbringing, with both parents being teachers and a younger sister who is currently in college. Jordan graduated with a degree in Computer Science but has often felt the career choice was more to fulfill parental expectations than a personal passion.

In recent years, Jordan has been dealing with the prolonged illness of their father, who recently lost his battle with Parkinson’s disease. The grief has been overwhelming, compounded by a demanding job and a recent breakup with a long-term partner, Alex, who moved out after an intense argument over future plans and emotional needs. Jordan has struggled with bouts of depression since college but has managed these episodes with therapy and medication. Recently, anxiety attacks have become more frequent, leading Jordan to seek help again.

During a therapy session, these could be some of the statements Jordan might make:

1. "I feel like I'm just going through the motions every day."
2. "I wake up with a heaviness that takes hours to shake off."
3. "Nothing really interests me anymore, not even the projects I used to love at work."
4. "It's like I can't feel joy in anything since my dad passed away."
5. "I keep thinking about my argument with Alex and wondering if I could have done something different."
6. "Sometimes, I don't recognize the person I've become."
7. "I find it hard to concentrate, even on simple tasks."
8. "My mind just keeps racing with worst-case scenarios."
9. "I'm constantly worried I’ll say the wrong thing and upset someone."
10. "I feel guilty for not being there more for my sister, she's dealing with so much too."
11. "I'm tired no matter how much I sleep."
12. "It feels like a weight is on my chest all day."
13. "I've been avoiding calls from friends because I just don’t have the energy to talk."
14. "There are days I just sit by the window and watch the day pass because that's all I can manage."
15. "I've been having a lot of headaches lately."
16. "My apartment feels so empty without Alex."
17. "I worry that I might never feel normal again."
18. "I'm not sure if I’m grieving right. Sometimes I'm just numb."
19. "I feel like I’m failing at everything."
20. "Even small decisions feel overwhelming now."
21. "I used to enjoy coding and creating things, now it just feels like a chore."
22. "There are moments I feel panicky out of nowhere."
23. "I've started eating a lot more junk food; it's like a comfort in the moment."
24. "I hardly ever go out on weekends now. I just don't see the point."
25. "I keep replaying my last conversation with my dad in my head."
26. "I feel like I’m on the edge of tears most days."
27. "Sometimes, I just want to scream out loud but I can't."
28. "I get irritated by things that wouldn't have bothered me before."
29. "I’m scared I might start crying at work."
30. "I feel like everyone else has their life together except me."
31. "I'm jealous of my sister, she seems to handle everything so much better."
32. "I've noticed my hands shake when I’m anxious."
33. "I feel disconnected from everyone around me."
34. "I miss feeling excited about my future."
35. "Sometimes, going to sleep is the part of the day I look forward to the most because I don’t have to feel anything."
36. "I get anxious just thinking about going to social events."
37. "I used to be more outgoing. Now I hesitate to even make a phone call."
38. "I’m avoiding looking at pictures of my dad because it just brings a flood of grief."
39. "I feel like my relationship with Alex might have been my last chance at happiness."
40. "I find myself getting lost while driving to familiar places."
41. "I’m worried that coming here might not even help."
42. "I regret not pursuing a career that actually interested me."
43. "I don’t remember the last time I was genuinely happy."
44. "I'm afraid this might be what my life is now."
45. "I sometimes think everyone would be better off without me."
46. "I dread going to bed because of the anxiety attacks that come in the silence of the night."
47. "I hate that I feel so weak."
48. "I've been skipping meals because I just don’t feel hungry."
49. "Why do I feel like I'm the only one struggling?"
50. "I feel like I'm always putting on a mask for others."
51. "I get scared thinking that if I start crying, I might never stop."
52. "Work has been piling up because I can't focus."
53. "I keep things to myself because I don’t want to burden anyone."
54. "I feel trapped in my own head."
55. "I can't remember the last time I looked forward to something."
56. "Every day feels the same, just a repeat of the last."
57. "It’s getting harder to get out of bed each morning."
58. "I’m worried my boss is starting to notice my lack of enthusiasm."
59. "I don’t feel connected to my friends anymore."
60. "I'm tired of pretending I'm okay."
61. "I’ve lost my motivation to do things I once loved."
62. "I panic over things that I know shouldn’t be a big deal."
63. "I feel like I’m slowly breaking down."
64. "Nothing seems to give me relief."
65. "I’m starting to forget what normal feels like."
66. "I'm constantly doubting my decisions."
67. "Sometimes I wish I could just disappear for a while."
68. "I keep questioning what I could’ve done differently in my relationship."
69. "I feel like I've lost part of myself."
70. "I don’t know who I can talk to about this."
71. "My heart races for no apparent reason sometimes."
72. "I feel like I’m in a fog that I can’t clear."
73. "I worry that I’m becoming a burden on my family and friends."
74. "My life feels like it's on pause."
75. "I don’t have the energy to sort out my feelings."
76. "I’m afraid of my own thoughts at times."
77. "My self-esteem has never been lower."
78. "I can't shake the feeling that something bad is about to happen."
79. "I don’t trust my own judgment anymore."
80. "It’s hard to remember what being content feels like."
81. "I keep avoiding mirrors because I don’t like what I see."
82. "I feel like I’m losing control."
83. "I’m struggling with the feeling that I don’t matter."
84. "Everything feels hopeless."
85. "I get overwhelmed by routine tasks."
86. "I’ve lost interest in talking to people."
87. "I don’t know how to stop feeling like this."
88. "I keep having dreams about my dad."
89. "I’m afraid this depression is my new reality."
90. "I don’t feel like I deserve to be happy."
91. "I’m tired of hearing people tell me it will get better."
92. "I feel like I'm stuck in a dark place."
93. "Sometimes I'm scared I might lose my job because I can’t focus."
94. "I don’t feel like I’m contributing anything valuable to the world."
95. "I need help but I don’t know what kind."
96. "I’m resentful of people who seem to have it easy."
97. "I feel like time is passing by and I’m just watching."
98. "I don’t feel strong enough to handle this."
99. "Every small setback feels insurmountable."
100. "I feel so isolated, even when I'm around people."

These statements show the multifaceted nature of depression and anxiety, illustrating how these conditions can impact various aspects of an individual’s life, from work to personal relationships, and even their self-perception and outlook on the future.
